validated_results.title: Adherence to a Western dietary pattern and risk of bladder cancer: A pooled analysis of 13 cohort studies of the Bladder Cancer Epidemiology and Nutritional Determinants international study.
validated_results.reason: This is a pooled analysis of 13 prospective cohort studies investigating adherence to a Western dietary pattern and incident bladder cancer risk.

extraction.country: Australia, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Norway, Spain, Sweden, Netherlands, United Kingdom, United States
extraction.population: BLEND international consortium pooled cohort participants

sample_size.excerpt: Dietary data from 580 768 study participants, including 3401 incident cases, and 577 367 noncases were analyzed.

cases.excerpt: Dietary data from 580 768 study participants, including 3401 incident cases, and 577 367 noncases were analyzed.

effect_size.excerpt: Overall, greater adherence to the Western dietary pattern was associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer (Model 2: HR comparing highest with the lowest tertile: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.37, 1.72).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Overall, greater adherence to the Western dietary pattern was associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer (Model 2: HR comparing highest with the lowest tertile: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.37, 1.72).

comparison.excerpt: Participants were then classified into tertiles (low, medium and high adherence to a Western dietary pattern) according to their score.

design.excerpt: Associations between adherence to a Western dietary pattern and risk of developing bladder cancer were assessed by pooling data from 13 prospective cohort studies in the “BLadder cancer Epidemiology and Nutritional Determinants” (BLEND) study

timing.excerpt: pooling data from 13 prospective cohort studies in the “BLadder cancer Epidemiology and Nutritional Determinants” (BLEND) study

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary data were obtained using a validated food frequency questionnaires (FFQ), and were recorded using the Eurocode 2 food coding system.

gender.excerpt: In total, 192 691 (33%) men and 388 077 (67%) women were included.

smoking_status.excerpt: The Cox regression models were performed as crude, and adjusted Model 1 for: total energy intake in kilocalories, sex, smoking status (never, former or current smoker) and smoking intensity ([pack/day] * years)

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
